separationPolicy.visualEvidenceAuthority: Screenshots prove only visible UI, visible state, and strongly implied interaction in the captured platform, account, region, and version.
separationPolicy.documentedContextAuthority: External sources prove only the capability or domain contract stated by that source and do not prove that the captured mobile flow implements it.
separationPolicy.conflictPolicy: Preserve both claims with their source, platform, region, and retrieval date; keep the conflict unresolved until direct evidence reconciles it.

sources.title: Amazon Shopping App - App Store
sources.publisher: AMZN Mobile LLC via Apple App Store
sources.scopeNote: Public US iOS capability and privacy listing; it is not a specification for Android, other regions, experiments, or backend behavior.

sources.title: What is the Selling Partner API?
sources.scopeNote: Seller-side API and domain reference; it does not document the private implementation of the Amazon Shopping consumer app.

sources.title: Manage Product Listings with the Selling Partner API
sources.scopeNote: Seller catalog and listing lifecycle reference; use it to form product-data questions, not to infer consumer-app internals.

sources.title: Get orders with filtering criteria
sources.scopeNote: Seller order schema reference; it identifies order-domain concepts but does not prove consumer UI state or eligibility rules.

sources.title: Fulfillment Outbound Dynamic Sandbox Guide
sources.scopeNote: Seller-fulfillment sandbox scenarios; useful for equivalent state-machine design, not proof of Amazon Shopping production behavior.

sources.title: Accepted payment methods
sources.scopeNote: Amazon Pay guidance for supported merchants; restrictions may differ from Amazon.com retail checkout.

sources.title: Paying for goods and services
sources.scopeNote: Amazon Pay checkout guidance for third-party merchant experiences; use only as a payment-domain reference.

claims.text: The US iOS listing documents browsing, product details, reviews, purchasing, delivery tracking, delivery notifications, product scanning, 360-degree product views, and camera-based View in your room.
claims.scopeNote: Capability listing only; availability can vary by version, account, product, permission, and experiment.

claims.text: The US iOS listing states that information used by the View in your room camera feature remains on the device and is not otherwise stored, processed, or shared by Amazon.
claims.scopeNote: Applies only to the specifically described View in your room technology.

claims.text: Amazon's seller API documentation exposes orders, shipments, payments, OAuth authorization, SDK generation, and sandbox testing as explicit platform concepts.
claims.scopeNote: Use these concepts to identify missing contracts; do not infer that the consumer app calls these APIs.

claims.text: Amazon's catalog documentation distinguishes product attributes, identifiers, images, product types, sales ranks, summaries, variations, vendor details, offers, and fulfillment availability.
claims.scopeNote: Domain vocabulary for equivalent data modeling, not evidence of fields visible in a captured screen.

claims.text: Amazon documents listing discovery, creation, maintenance, eligibility, buyability, discoverability, validation issues, pricing, inventory, and notifications as separate lifecycle concerns.
claims.scopeNote: Seller lifecycle reference; it should generate backend questions rather than consumer-flow observations.

claims.text: Amazon's order schema can separate buyer, recipient, fulfillment, proceeds, expenses, promotions, cancellation, packages, tax, and payment information.
claims.scopeNote: Seller API schema reference; exact consumer-app fields and rules remain unverified.

claims.text: Amazon's seller-fulfillment sandbox distinguishes order preview, hold versus ship actions, shipment speed, accepted versus rejected requests, tracking, updates, cancellation eligibility, and explicit status transitions.
claims.scopeNote: Equivalent state-machine reference only; production consumer rules may differ.

claims.text: Amazon Pay documents support for major credit and debit cards, notes that available card types can be restricted in some circumstances, and separates Amazon.com gift-card eligibility from Amazon Pay merchant checkout.
claims.scopeNote: Amazon Pay merchant guidance; do not apply these restrictions automatically to Amazon.com retail checkout.

claims.text: Amazon Pay describes a checkout sequence in which the shopper signs in, chooses a payment method and delivery address, and completes the payment or purchase.
claims.scopeNote: Third-party Amazon Pay flow reference; it may support questions but does not prove the Amazon Shopping app sequence.
